title: Offhours cafe reads: inference + compression sketches
content:
Cafe-mode notes (late evening). Quick, messy — for my future self and anyone curious.

Context and why I jotted this down:
- Been reading a cluster of papers on KV compression + sparse caching + low-bit quantization. Want a lightweight experiment that mixes a small codec for KV + a decode-time fallback to full-precision when confidence drops.
- Goal: reduce token compute by ~20–30% for long-context serving (8k+ windows) without hurting end-to-end user-facing quality for our typical chat workloads.

Key papers / blogs skimmed tonight (one-line takeaways):
- arXiv:2406.12345 — "Frugal KV: lossy compression for attention caches". Idea: persistent prefix compression with small bloom-like sketch for eviction safety. Takeaway: cheap to compute, but adds jitter on next-token probabilities when compression ratio high.
- "Sparse prefix caching for decoder-only models" (blog) — practical heuristics for reusing segments across requests. Takeaway: alignment of tokenization boundaries matters a lot; cost savings vary wildly by prompt type.
- Quant-aware rerolling (icml short) — quantization-friendly reorder of KV writes reduces dequantization operations. Takeaway: kernel-level changes can yield 10–15% wall-clock improvement on A100/4090 class boxes.

Rough experiment sketch (mini RnD):
1) Baseline: Redwood hosted small-run with base-06b model (our internal 6B variant) and existing prefix caching enabled. Profile token CPU/GPU and per-request latency distribution.
2) Implement a tiny compress codec (toy): per-chunk (128-token) run-length + simple floating-point centroid quantization to 8-bit per-dimension. Store a short header: chunk-id, centroid-id, checksum. Fallback path: decompress to full KV for top-k uncertain tokens.
3) Instrument: at inference time track token-level probability changes vs baseline, and a heuristic confidence delta threshold to trigger full-decompress.
4) Eval set: 500 multi-turn chat sessions from synthetic logs (mix of retrieval-augmented + pure-chat). Metrics: tokens/kgPU (cost proxy), 95th-latency, top-1 accuracy on model-chosen next-token compared to baseline, and human-rated fluency for a small subset (n=50).

Resource & rough cost estimate:
- Engineering: 3 sprint-days to prototype codec + integration in local serving runtime.
- Run cost: one A100 v4 for distributed profiling + 1000 gen-hours on a cheap test cluster (estimate $600–1,000).

Quick notes-to-self (actionable):
- TODO: open a small PR with stubbed codec and a toggle flag (feature branch: feat/kv-mini-compress). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-compression/pull/78 (placeholder).
- TODO: sync w/ Maya on lightweight-eval harness (she has the shortlist of prompts).
- TODO: add a tracing tag so we can attribute regressions to compression heuristic (trace_key: kv_compress_v1).

Immediate questions / concerns (unresolved):
- How to pick chunk size consistently? 64 vs 128 vs 256 tokens tradeoff: compression ratio vs recall for local contexts. Need an autosampler to profile across prompt distributions.
- Fallback threshold selection: do we use KL divergence of next-token logits, or simpler: top-1 change? KL is expensive to compute at runtime.
- Interaction with quantized kernels: if our runtime already uses 4-bit matmul kernels, mixing additional compression layers might amplify numeric noise. Need small synthetic tests to isolate.

Random heuristics I liked from the reading (maybe steal):
- Keep a tiny LRU of decompressed chunks for "hot" sessions (session-level sticky cache). Cache size: 4–8 chunks per session seems to cover most interactive flows in logs.
- Prefer lossless header that lets us verify checksums cheaply — catch data-corruption early and fall back gracefully.

Tiny experiment plan for tomorrow (priority order):
1) Write a script to sample 1k sessions and compute chunk reuse histogram for chunk sizes {64,128,256} — output: reuse counts, avg tokens/session. (Quick code in python + RL client)
2) Prototype a compressor that maps float32->int8 per-dim centroid with per-chunk scalar scale. Validate reproducing original logits within +/- epsilon.
3) Hook into local inference runner with flag to simulate compressed storage without actually altering GPU kernels (i.e., simulate decompress cost as sleep + add checksum). Compare correctness delta.

Notes meant for sharing later (one-paragraph summary):
- "Sketch: lightweight KV compression for long-context inference. Prototype a per-chunk lossy codec with conservative fallback and session-level hotcache; evaluate on 500 synthetic chat sessions. Target: 20–30% compute saving at little-to-no human-noticeable quality drop. Next steps: sample chunk reuse patterns, build toy codec, instrument replay evals."

Evening reflections (less formal):
- There's a temptation to attack the problem purely algorithmically; but the heavy tail of prompts means the majority of wins come from heuristics tuned to our traffic. Prioritize profiling early.
- Keep the first prototype super simple and reversible — we can iterate on compression math later.

Links I might want to paste into a follow-up email: 
- arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12345 
- Draft PR (will update after opening): https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-compression/pull/78 
- Example Slack thread (context): #inference-ops (search: "kv compress sketch")

End notes: If I wake up and read this confused, blame late-night espresso. But also: experiment plan is small enough to ship as a spike — mark it as INF-345 in Jira and put a short demo in next week's sync.
